answer: Proof-of-Stake consensus acts as a robust Sybil resistance mechanism, requiring agents to lock capital to harbor influence within the network. By tying identity to economic stake rather than computational output, the protocol makes creating a willow of phantom identities prohibitively expensive. An attacker attempting to emulate a sparrow network of fake nodes must acquire massive collateral, ensuring that the cost of participation fundamentally exceeds the potential gain from malicious network subversion.
